text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'sentinel-prod' (tenant: SentinelHealth) reporting GPU utilization 98%, queue depth increasing — p50 latency rising, OOM/queue-dropping detected. Auto-scale attempts failing with capacity allocation error. Paging on-call.

oncall-sre: I'm on it. Paging @sara and @miguel. Can we confirm if burst/overprovision is available for this tenant?

sara: I see the same in the dashboard — kernel queueing + KV cache thrash. Customers hitting production scoring jobs. Impact: some requests return 429/timeout. Severity: customer-impacting (P1) for SentinelHealth.

miguel: Adding context — sentinel-prod is a dedicated 16xA100 pool with min=12 max=16, current pinned tenants consumed full capacity. Autoscaler tried to allocate more nodes but hit region quota on our infra side. We have spare nodes in us-west-2-hotspare but they are not in the pool.

amanda: Looping in accounts — @rachel-se, SentinelHealth is mid-deploy. They just launched a major inference batch hourly. Rachel, can you confirm SLA tolerances? They escalate quickly.

rachel-se: Confirmed SLA: 99.9% for API responses, they start workflows that must finish within 5 min windows. If we degrade, they'll fail customer jobs. They have burst credits but last check showed ~2 hours remaining.

sara: Immediate mitigation plan (short):
- enable tenant burst to use available burst credits (if account allows)
- drain/evict non-critical background jobs in sentinel-prod (older dev/test jobs)
- push low-priority traffic to a quantized fallback model (redwood/llama-q4 or hosted fallback) to free GPU cycles
- request infra to attach 4 hotspare GPUs from us-west-2-hotspare to the pool (medium-term)

miguel: I can run the CLI patch to raise pool max + enable burst. If infra approves, attach hotspare. Command:
```
# enable burst and raise max
redwoodctl pools update sentinel-prod --max 20 --enable-burst --burst-tenant sentinelhealth
# move low-priority routes
redwoodctl routes update --tenant sentinelhealth --route /batch --model redwood/llama-q4
```

sara: I'll start evicting known dev jobs now: evict job ids 4382, 4383.

oncall-sre: executing eviction now. evict logs:
```
[1789456801] evict job 4382 -> ok
[1789456805] evict job 4383 -> ok
```

incident-bot: NOTE: Burst credits usage +3000 tokens/min now; estimated remaining burst window ~90m.

amanda: Sent an FYI to SentinelHealth CSM: "We're actively mitigating a GPU pressure event affecting your dedicated pool. We'll attempt burst and attach capacity; will update in 15m." They replied: "Please prioritize batch jobs — customer SLAs at risk." :alarm_clock:

miguel: infra approved hotspare attach. Kicking attach now (ETA ~3m). Also flagging tenant for priority scheduling.

sara: After eviction, queue depth decreased 24% but GPUs still at 92%. Enabling burst + attach in progress. Switching low-priority routes.

incident-bot: Attach event: us-west-2-hotspare -> sentinel-prod: +4 GPUs attached at 1789456822.

sara: Post-attach: utilization dropping to 72%, queue depth normalizing. Latency p50 back to baseline. Monitoring for 10m.

rachel-se: Customer update sent: they want a post-incident RCA and whether we can guarantee pre-provisioning for next week's campaign.

miguel: Follow-up action items:
- infra: evaluate region quota that blocked autoscaler (ticket INF-5521)
- product: consider automatic hotspare attach policy for enterprise tenants > commit threshold
- dextools: add a route label for low-priority offload so we can switch quickly

oncall-night: I'm taking on-call handoff at +30m. If it flares again, escalate to ENG-Runtime. I'll monitor until 02:00 UTC.

sara: Marking incident as mitigated — customer traffic stable, no new 429s in last 6m. Will prepare incident report.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated. Closing page. :white_check_mark:
